caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 429 of 2008.
lawyer:
Md Ibrahim Khalil, Advocate-on-Record-----For the Petitioner.
Not Represented-----For the Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Jabbar ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Akter Hossain Bhuiyan and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 3-1-2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1480 of 1997).
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J : This petition for leave to appeal is against the judgment and order dated 3-1-2006 passed in Civil Revision No 1480 of 1997 by the High Court Division discharging the Rule, which was issued against the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 107 of 1994 by the Court of Additional District Judge, Munshiganj, allowing the appeal setting-aside the judgment and decree dated 27-7-1994 passed in Title Suit No. 34 of 1989 by the 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Munshiganj, dismissing the suit filed for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession.

2. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 34 of 1989 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Munshiganj, for declaration of title and for khas possession. The plaintiff's case in short is that one Kademunnessa Khatun was the superior landlord of the suit land and Salim Khan, Alep Khan and Fazil Khan, sons of Baru Khan, were bargadars under the said landlord and the same has been correctly recorded in the CS Khatian. Afterwards, the said bargadars handed over the said lands to the Zamindar's Seresta. Abdur Razzak, the son of the said Kademunnessa sold out lands in the suit plot No. 42 to Shamsuddin Bhuiyan alias Raja Mia, father of the plaintiff appellants, by registered sale deed dated 19-12-1942 and delivered possession thereof and later Abdul Kashem Sona Mia and Golam Saber Shamsuddin Ahmed grandsons of Kademunnessa became owner-possessors of suit plot No. 41 on basis of a gift and while thus they were owning and possessing the same, they sold out the said land of Plot No. 41 to aforesaid Shamsuddin Bhuiyan and at the relevant time vendor Golam Saber Shamsuddin Ahmed being minor, the patta deed dated 1-7-1944 was executed and registered by his father, the natural guardian, and accordingly said Shamsuddin Bhuiyan has been possessing as owner of the suit plots and enjoying usufructs therefrom on payment of rates and taxes to the Sheresta of the Zaminder and, after withdrawal of the Zamindari System, said Shamsuddin Bhuiyan became a tenant directly under the government pursuant to the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, was owning and possessing the suit lands on payment of rates and taxes to the government and that in the SA Khatian, along with the name of Shamsuddin Bhuiyan wrongly the names of aforesaid Salim, Alep and Fazil Khan appeared, and that said Salim, Alep and Fazil Khan did never claimed ownership or possession on the suit plots and they did not pay any rents ever to the government in respect of the suit land. After the death of Shamsuddin Bhuiyan and his wife Rahima Begum, their three sons, the plaintiffs, and one daughter inherited the properties left, including the suit land and on amicable partition, amongst themselves, the plaintiffs got the suit land in their saham and thus became the exclusive owner-possessors of the suit land and were enjoying usufructs there from through Bargader, since they were in employment at different places, and that the plaintiff No. 1 on his retirement, is possessing the suit land and cultivating the same with his own men and that on 9-8-1987 the defendant No. 1, taking advantage of the wrong recording of the names of said Salim Khan and others in the SA Khatian along with real owner Shamsuddin Bhuiyan, claimed the suit land alleging inter alia that father of the defendant No. 1 Abdul Jabbar on 18-3-1984 purchased the suit land from the heirs the SA recorded tenants namely Salim Khan and his two brothers and threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land and that faced with such situation the plaintiffs filed criminal case in the Court of Magistrate, who upon hearing dismissed the case holding the defendant to be in possession of the suit land and that the plaintiff also lost in the appeal filed against the order passed by the Magistrate, however as per observation made by the appellate Court, the plaintiffs filed the suit. The defendant contested the suit denying ownership and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land relying on purchase made by his father. The plaintiffs adduced four (4) witnesses and produced documents marked Exhibits-1 to 4 series in support of their case and the defendant adduced five (5) witnesses and produced documents marked Ka to Gha series in support of his case Five (5) issues were framed and the suit was dismissed holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land as well as their story of dispossession from the suit land. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 107 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge, Munshiganj, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge allowing the appeal and setting-aside the decree passed by the trial Court and thereby decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 22-3-1997 declaring the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land and ordered for recovery of khas possession and that the defendant-respondents being aggrieved moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1480 of 1997 and Rule issued therein was heard and disposed of by the judgment and order discharging the Rule, which has been impugned in his leave petition.

<u>3. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on detailed discussion of the materials available in the records of the case and that it has been observed that :—</u>

<u>"Mr Md Shafiqul Islam Dhali the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite-party in reply submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, firstly committed error of law in misreading the Exhibit 3, registered deed of sale dated 1-8-1989 executed by CS recorded Zamindar Akkas Uddin in favour of Hazetun Nessa transferring the rent receiving interest of the suit land along with other land, inasmuch as, the same being a registered deed of sale executed and registered about 90 years old and negative presumption of the same could only be formed through evidence keeping in view of the development and circumstances consequent to the execution and registration thereof till the present. Mr. Dhali next submits that the plaintiffs exhibited as many as 20 rent receipts out of them some were issued by Zaminder and 18 of them issued by the Government, being Exhibit 4 series proved the payment of rent in respect of the suit land till 1988 by the plaintiff and also proved the possession and enjoyment of the suit property by the plaintiffs and further standing of collateral evidence of title of the plaintiffs in support of his contention, but the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in his judgment mentioned that the plaintiffs exhibited only 2 rent receipt and thereby proceeded towards by the erroneous decision in support of his contention Mr Dhali relies on the decision of our. Appellate Division reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216 wherein it has been held that rent receipts through not documents of title, are not items of evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows of title. Mr Dhali further submits that SA Khatian being Exhibits Kha(2) and Kha(3) and RS Khatian finally published being recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively although one of the two SA Khatian being Exhibit Kha(2) contained the name of the CS recorded tenants along with the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff. In this connection Mr Dhali submits that it is settled principle of law that the last record of right will prevail than the earlier record of right, in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 35 DLR 295 and 17 DLR 392 and 27 DLR 589 relying on the decision of a Division Bench of this Court reported in 42 DLR 434. Mr Dhali submits that RS Khatian prepared under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has the presumption of correctness under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Mr Dhali finally submits that although the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge is not lengthy but the learned Additional District Judge refers the Judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge adverting the material findings of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and discussed the oral and documentary evidence in doing so and that there is no misreading of any evidence on record and neither there is any non-consideration of material evidence on record on the part of the learned Additional District Judge and that being so the Additional District Judge being appellate Court and thereby being the final Court of facts, its judgment is not liable to be interfered with."</u>

<u>And thus found that the trial Court arrived at its wrong decision because of non-consideration of the material evidences on record, namely the rent receipts granted by the government marked Exhibits-4 series and the deed dated 1-8-1899, a 90 years old registered deed as well as the SA Khatian and RS Khatian, standing in names of the predecessor-in-interest and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively, marked Exhibits-Kha(2) and Kha(3). We do not find any reason of differ with the same.</u>

4. In view of our discussion and observation made above, and having regard to the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Erfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Mia, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216, we are of the opinion that the High Court Division has passed the impugned judgment and order in accordance with law on due consideration of the materials on record and hence no interference is called for.

Accordingly the application for leave to appeal is dismissed without costs.

End.
